title: ID0445430-DC/Si-D/AT-[Y2/RN300000003010] 0kWh Charging session
description:

Solution: 3 possibilities:
- XD10.1 or XD10.3 loose
- StateMonitor failure
- Contactors not closing

additional_info.subject: Issue Description
additional_info.body:
Hello,
I previously made a ticket (ID0443148) where it was said that the
charger didn't have any issue and that it seemed to have been an
issue on Sifinity Control's side.
I held the charger under supervision on our side through OCPP and
I've noticed that there were only charging sessions with a load of
0,000kWh since 19.08.2025, as seen in the attached pictures.
Could you please check again what is wrong with the charger?
As there were multiple tries to charge from different customers
with different cars, we don't think that it was a problem with the
cars.

additional_info.subject: ID0445430-DC/Si-D/AT-[Y2/RN300000003010] Connectors Are Faulted CRM:02699000199
additional_info.body:
Hi Johannes, good morning.
I checked the logs and we need to confirm which of the components is faulty, I suspect:
XD10.1 and XD10.3
Contactors
StateMonitor
I can see in the logs the following, right after we reach CableCheck:
I assume that this was a StateMonitor issue as it's very hard that both contactors failed at the same time, except for the XDs.
The next time this occurs, please proceed to measure if the contactors are closing properly and the busbar to confirm if voltage is going through. Even though we might have 24V between A1 and A2, it might not be closing properly.
If the contactors are closing properly, then we should also check via TF1/TF2 if the voltage readings are correct. The TFs share the same XD10.1 and XD10.3 so it might be related.
The line of thought here is, if it's not XD10.1 or XD10.3, then it must be the contactors or the StateMonitor.
I would recommend going for the StateMonitor first if it's not the XD10s and only after replace QAs.
I will forward this to RC-AT queue.
Thanks!
Best regards,
Francisco
